velocity_method.description: Velocity-method selector used by the SimulationConfig schema. Currently only `Waterloo` is accepted here. SSP&A workflows still use `Waterloo` in the config because the SSP&A velocity field is fitted outside the JSON config and then tracked through the same runtime interface.

solver.description: Runge-Kutta solver variant for particle integration. `Euler` uses a fixed step (non-adaptive). `Rk4StepDoubling` is a classic RK4 with step-doubling error control. `DormandPrince` is the recommended default (embedded 4/5 pair). `CashKarp` is an alternative 4/5 pair. `VernerRobust` and `VernerEfficient` are 5/6 pairs (6th-order solution, 5th-order error estimate) for high-accuracy work.

adaptive.description: Adaptive time-stepping parameters that control how the solver adjusts dt between integration steps. All fields are required even when using the non-adaptive Euler solver.

tolerance.description: Local truncation error threshold for step acceptance. The solver compares its embedded-pair error estimate against this value; steps with error ≤ tolerance are accepted. The error is measured as a fraction of the model extent in each direction. Smaller values produce more accurate trajectories but require more (smaller) steps. Typical starting value: 1e-6.

safety.description: Safety factor (S) applied when computing the next step size: h_new = h × S × (tol/err)^alpha. Values < 1 (typically 0.8–0.95) make step-size growth conservative, reducing the chance of immediate rejection on the next step. Recommended: 0.9.

alpha.description: Exponent in the step-scaling formula h_new = h × S × (tol/err)^alpha. Derived from the solver order: for a pair of orders p and p+1, the usual value is 1/(p+1). Use 0.2 for the 4th/5th-order pairs (DormandPrince, CashKarp) and for Rk4StepDoubling, and 1/6 (about 0.167) for the 5th/6th-order Verner pairs.

min_scale.description: Minimum allowed step-size scaling factor. After a rejected step the new dt cannot shrink below min_scale × current dt. Prevents pathological collapse of the step size. Typical value: 0.2 (step can shrink to at most 1/5th).

max_scale.description: Maximum allowed step-size scaling factor. After an accepted step the new dt cannot grow beyond max_scale × current dt. Prevents overshooting into a region where the step would be rejected. Typical value: 5.0.

max_rejects.description: Maximum number of consecutive rejected steps before the solver terminates the particle with an error. Increase this (e.g. to 50) if particles encounter sharp velocity gradients that need many successive reductions. Default recommendation: 10.

min_dt.description: Absolute minimum time step in model time units. If the adaptive algorithm needs a step smaller than this, the particle terminates with an error, unless adaptive.euler_dt is at least this large; one Euler step of that size is then taken instead. Set small enough to handle tight regions but large enough to prevent the solver from stalling indefinitely. Typical value: 1e-10.

euler_dt.description: Threshold of the adaptive solvers' emergency Euler step. If the step size shrinks to this value or below, the solver takes a forward-Euler step of this size, with no error control, so it acts as a floor on the step size. Set it equal to min_dt. The Euler solver does not use it; it steps at initial_dt. In model time units.

relocate_stages.description: When true, each Runge-Kutta stage finds the cell that contains it, as mod-PATH3DU does at every stage; when false, all stages of a step use the cell at the start of the step. Optional; default true.

dispersion.description: Dispersion model configuration. Choose `None` for pure advection, `Gsde` for the generalised stochastic differential equation method, or `Ito` for the Itô-calculus formulation. When dispersion is enabled, each particle run is stochastic — run multiple realisations (Monte Carlo) to build concentration fields. The dispersivities are given either here (alpha_l, alpha_th and alpha_tv, all three, the same in every cell) or per cell to hydrate_cell_properties() or hydrate_sspa_inputs(), never both: with dispersion on, a run that gives them both ways, or neither, stops with an error.

method.description: Disables dispersion. Particles follow pure advective streamlines.
Generalised Stochastic Differential Equation dispersion method.

alpha_l.description: Longitudinal dispersivity — spreading along the flow direction, in model length units (e.g. metres). Usually the largest of the three. Give all three of alpha_l, alpha_th and alpha_tv, for the same dispersivities in every cell, or none of them, with the dispersivities given per cell instead.

alpha_th.description: Horizontal transverse dispersivity — spreading perpendicular to flow in the horizontal plane, in model length units. Give all three of alpha_l, alpha_th and alpha_tv, for the same dispersivities in every cell, or none of them, with the dispersivities given per cell instead.

alpha_tv.description: Vertical transverse dispersivity — spreading perpendicular to flow in the vertical direction, in model length units. Typically the smallest of the three; must be 0 with an SSP&A (MEUK) field, which is two-dimensional. Give all three of alpha_l, alpha_th and alpha_tv, for the same dispersivities in every cell, or none of them, with the dispersivities given per cell instead.

alpha_l.description: Longitudinal dispersivity — spreading along the flow direction, in model length units (e.g. metres). Usually the largest of the three. Give all three of alpha_l, alpha_th and alpha_tv, for the same dispersivities in every cell, or none of them, with the dispersivities given per cell instead. Per-cell dispersivities must be the same in every cell for Ito.

alpha_th.description: Horizontal transverse dispersivity — spreading perpendicular to flow in the horizontal plane, in model length units. Give all three of alpha_l, alpha_th and alpha_tv, for the same dispersivities in every cell, or none of them, with the dispersivities given per cell instead. Per-cell dispersivities must be the same in every cell for Ito.

alpha_tv.description: Vertical transverse dispersivity — spreading perpendicular to flow in the vertical direction, in model length units. Typically the smallest of the three; must be 0 with an SSP&A (MEUK) field, which is two-dimensional. Give all three of alpha_l, alpha_th and alpha_tv, for the same dispersivities in every cell, or none of them, with the dispersivities given per cell instead. Per-cell dispersivities must be the same in every cell for Ito.

retardation_enabled.description: Reserved for retardation, which MP3DU-RS does not apply yet: the value has no effect. (mod-PATH3DU's RETARDATION option multiplies each cell's porosity by its retardation factor.)

max_time.description: Maximum cumulative tracking time for one particle, in the model's time units (for example days or seconds). The last step is shortened so that tracking stops when the accumulated travel time reaches this value.

max_steps.description: Maximum number of accepted integration steps for one particle. This is unitless and acts as a safety cap on solver work even if the particle has not yet been captured or reached max_time.

stagnation_velocity.description: Velocity-magnitude threshold used for stagnation detection, in model length per model time (for example m/day or ft/s). A step is counted as stagnant when the particle velocity magnitude is below this value.

stagnation_limit.description: Number of consecutive stagnant accepted steps required before termination. If velocity rises back above stagnation_velocity, the stagnation counter resets to zero.

capture_radius.description: Distance from the well centre (cell centre) used for internal-well capture. A particle is terminated only after it gets within this radius of the centre. Smaller values delay capture until the particle is very near the centre; larger values make capture occur sooner after entering the well cell. Omit it, or set it to null, to capture a particle as soon as it enters the well cell.

face_epsilon.description: Tolerance for top/bottom face proximity checks during IFACE-based capture. Particle is considered at the face when z > 1 - face_epsilon (top) or z < face_epsilon (bottom). Increase only if particles leak through top/bottom capture faces; decrease only if they are being captured too far from the face. Default: 1e-6.

initial_dt.description: Starting time step for the first integration step of each particle, in model time units. The adaptive solver will adjust this after the first step. The Euler solver uses it as its fixed step, capped at max_dt.

max_dt.description: Upper bound on the time step in model time units. The adaptive solver will never grow dt beyond this value, even if the error estimate would allow it. Prevents particles from jumping over cells in smooth regions.

direction.description: Tracking direction. Use 1.0 for forward tracking (particles move downgradient / in the direction of flow) or -1.0 for backward tracking (particles move upgradient / against the flow direction). No other value is accepted; 1 and -1 written as integers are the same values and are accepted.
